Tubes and ribbons along curves

Source: R/layers-sweep.R
geom_tube_3d.Rd

Sweeps a circle (tubes) or a line segment (ribbons) along each group's path in the order of the rows, in transformed position units. The cross section lies in the plane of a rotation-minimising frame, computed by the double reflection method of Wang et al. (2008), so it does not spin about the curve the way a Frenet frame does, and does not flip at inflections. On a closed curve (closed = TRUE) the frame carried once around the curve would miss its starting orientation by an angle; that angle is spread over the curve in proportion to arc length, so the surface closes without a seam.

Usage

geom_tube_3d(
  mapping = NULL,
  data = NULL,
  position = "identity",
  ...,
  sides = 16L,
  radius = NULL,
  radius.unit = "data",
  cap = c("round", "flat", "none"),
  closed = FALSE,
  spline = NULL,
  n = 100L,
  na.rm = FALSE,
  show.legend = NA,
  inherit.aes = TRUE
)

geom_ribbon_3d(
  mapping = NULL,
  data = NULL,
  position = "identity",
  ...,
  width = NULL,
  width.unit = "data",
  normal = c(0, 0, 1),
  closed = FALSE,
  spline = NULL,
  n = 100L,
  na.rm = FALSE,
  show.legend = NA,
  inherit.aes = TRUE
)

Arguments

mapping, data, position, ..., na.rm, show.legend, inherit.aes

Standard layer arguments.

sides

Number of points on the tube's circle.

radius, width

Cross-section size where the aesthetic is not mapped.

radius.unit, width.unit

Unit of the cross-section size: "data" (transformed position units) or "mm" (millimetres on the page).

cap

End caps of a tube on an open curve: "round", "flat" or "none".

closed

Whether the path is a closed loop.

spline

NULL, or a stat_spline_3d() type to smooth the path first.

n

Number of spline samples.

normal

Direction the first cross section is oriented towards: the ribbon's surface normal, or the profile's first axis in stat_sweep_3d().

Value

A ggplot2 layer.

Details

The radius (tubes) or width (ribbons) aesthetic varies the cross section per point, and twist turns it about the curve by that many degrees. Without either, the size is the radius or width parameter, by default 2% (tubes) or 8% (ribbons) of the diagonal of the position ranges. Tube ends are closed with hemispheres (cap = "round") or disks ("flat"), or left open ("none"). A ribbon starts with its surface normal as close to normal as the curve allows.

Numeric aesthetics such as a continuous fill are taken at every point and averaged over each face, so they change gradually from ring to ring. spline passes the points through stat_spline_3d() first, with n samples. Normals are angle-weighted and split where faces meet at more than 60 degrees. Computed variables: arc_length from the first point and z_mean.

With radius.unit = "mm" (width.unit for ribbons) the size is measured on the page, like a line width: the cross section is swept when the plot is drawn, in the box the camera sees, so a tube is round on screen whatever the box proportions and has its radius in millimetres at the centre of the view, shrinking with distance under a perspective camera, as millimetre spheres of geom_sphere_3d() do. Sizes then default to 1 mm (tube radius) and 4 mm (ribbon width), and z_mean is the height of the curve point. Millimetre sizes need the Euclidean coordinates of coord_3d().

References

Wang, Juettler, Zheng and Liu (2008). Computation of rotation minimizing frames. ACM Transactions on Graphics 27, 2. doi:10.1145/1330511.1330513

Examples

t <- seq(0, 4 * pi, length.out = 120)
helix <- data.frame(x = cos(t), y = sin(t), z = t / 4, t = t)
ggplot2::ggplot(helix, ggplot2::aes(x, y, z = z, fill = t)) +
  geom_tube_3d(radius = 0.12) + coord_3d()
knot <- data.frame(u = seq(0, 2 * pi, length.out = 13)[-13])
knot <- transform(knot, x = sin(u) + 2 * sin(2 * u), y = cos(u) - 2 * cos(2 * u), z = -sin(3 * u))
ggplot2::ggplot(knot, ggplot2::aes(x, y, z = z)) +
  geom_tube_3d(radius = 0.3, closed = TRUE, spline = "catmull-rom", n = 200) + coord_3d()
ggplot2::ggplot(helix, ggplot2::aes(x, y, z = z, twist = t * 20)) +
  geom_ribbon_3d(width = 0.4) + coord_3d()
ggplot2::ggplot(helix, ggplot2::aes(x, y, z = z, fill = t)) +
  geom_tube_3d(radius = 1.5, radius.unit = "mm") + coord_3d(aspect = c(3, 1, 1))
